name: CROWS
summary: A microwave implementation of light shining through a wall, searching for weakly coupled light particles with highly isolated resonant cavities.
detection_principle: Microwaves in an emitting cavity can convert to hidden photons or axions, cross a barrier and regenerate in a receiving cavity; electromagnetic shielding rejects ordinary leakage.

status.label: The documented historical experimental phase is complete
status.evidence: 2013 sources support the phase recorded here, rather than a real-time status of the entire project as of the access date.

timeline.event: First results of the CERN Resonant WISP Search (CROWS)

collaboration.name: CROWS Collaboration / project team
collaboration.participants_note: Only documented principal institutions are listed; full author and affiliation lists are in the sources. Collaborating-institution addresses are not substituted for detector locations.

key_parameters.name: Representative masses studied
key_parameters.value: Axions approximately 7.2 μeV; hidden photons approximately 10.8 μeV

results.summary: Published coupling-exclusion limits; the targets are laboratory-produced particles, rather than Galactic-halo flux.

science_scope: Produces and detects axions or dark-sector particles in the laboratory, rather than directly measuring Galactic-halo dark-matter flux. It tests interactions of dark-matter candidates; identifying a discovered particle as dark matter would also require establishing its cosmic abundance.
